question: Why do children who used to say went correctly start saying goed?
answer: Because they have learned a rule. At first went is stored whole; once a child extracts add -ed for the past, the rule sometimes overrides the memory. Such errors are rare, a few per cent of irregular past tenses in recorded speech. Goed is a mistake only a rule-learner can make.
move: A new kind of error can be the sign of a new skill.
ask: When I or someone else makes a new kind of mistake, could it signal a new skill?
reference: Marcus, Pinker, Ullman, Hollander, Rosen & Xu, Overregularization in Language Acquisition, Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development, 1992
